entities.summary:
Atticus (b. 150 CE) was a philosopher or thinker of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Global. He is known for his work in the fields of philosophers & thinkers.

Atticus was a prominent figure in the philosophical circles of Rome, where he engaged in debates with notable thinkers such as Epictetus and Seneca. His teachings emphasized the importance of living in accordance with nature and cultivating inner strength.

Atticus's ideas had a significant impact on the development of Stoicism, a school of thought that emphasizes reason, self-control, and indifference to external events. His writings, although not surviving in their entirety, have been influential in shaping the philosophical landscape of the ancient world.

The legacy of Atticus can be seen in the many philosophical schools and traditions that followed in his footsteps, including the Stoics, Epicureans, and Skeptics.

'A wise man is the one who makes himself worthy of life, not by the quality of his life, but by the quality of his death.' - Atticus
